reviews.text: Has Gone Downhill. I started using Clue over a decade ago and quit tracking with it a couple years ago. I keep it on my phone because of all the data that they still have, but it makes me so sad to see how downhill it has gone. What once felt like an app that tried to empower its users now feels like its main purpose is to get their money. An app that used to center education and an easy to use experience is now impossible to use for even 10 seconds without encountering full-screen pop-ups asking you to subscribe. I might be willing to pay for the service if they weren’t so incessant about the experience for those who can’t or aren’t willing to pay being terrible (when it was quite the opposite in the past). The education they used to seemingly pride themselves on is now largely locked behind a paywall. Things I used to track that felt important to me (including breast pain as someone who had a scare at a young age) are now locked behind a paywall. Articles that were useful when I first started using the app as a young girl just starting to learn about her body are now locked. While I’m now an adult (who was considering using the app again as I begin trying to conceive and was quickly reminded why I stopped using it in the first place), it makes me feel a bit sad to think that the resource I once had in this app no longer exists for young people (or anyone of any age who maybe needs information that is more readily accessible without having to pay for it). Of course I understand most things have moved to a subscription model now, and of course things need money to continue running and developing, but it feels like every time I open this app they’ve locked something else behind a paywall, and there are somehow more ads asking me to pay for an app I’ve barely opened. What I notice is largely features that have existed for as long as I’ve been using the app continuing to be locked, rather than tons of new features (which feels more reasonable). But what bothers me the most is how much of the education is locked, that was once so helpful to me as a young person. It feels so against what the folks who designed this app once claimed they stood for, that it’s the reason I won’t even consider paying for it. It feels so disingenuous.

Education or disclaimers that accompany “your period is late” notifications about how the timing of your ovulation impacts the length of your cycle could be helpful for reducing stress. Pay to play.. I used Clue years ago and went through a couple of years where I didn’t need it (expected side effect from endometriosis medication- amenorrhea), but I’ve returned to it as my circumstances have changed. 

I hate it. I don’t like having the paid subscription shoved in my face multiple times every time I use the app, and I feel the app is now bloated with extra clutter, especially for free users. It wasn’t the case before, but now the screen for recording period symptoms shows me a 50/50 of usable vs. unusable features. I ALSO really don’t like that I can’t permanently decline the banner ads for smart devices I won’t be buying. There is no reason for me to be asked MONTHLY (because you can hide the banner- but only for a month) if I want to spend ~$300 for a tracker that ALSO requires a subscription to get full use of. Even after ignoring 5+ banners IN A ROW, there’s still a permanent banner begging me to try the subscription, as if I could possibly forget that it’s an option with the number of padlock icons shown next to unusable modules. 

The wheel layout for the monthly cycle calendar is still great and I like that tracking is a few button taps- AFTER I’ve gone through the list of options and unchecked at least half of them. The app works as advertised so I feel like a one star review is unfair, but, as I said, the interface feels bloated and cluttered. If you’re willing to pay for it and you have one of the trackers with integration or you’re interested in tracking pregnancy/perimenopause, it may be worth it, but I don’t think it’s worth the download otherwise.
